mainTopic: Torah as the remedy for the יצר הרע, a father's duties to his son, and honoring and fearing parents
overview: This עמוד of קידושין begins by finishing a chain of פסוקים showing that Torah should be sharp and ready in a person's mouth. Study partners who argue fiercely, even a father and son, end up loving each other. A ברייתא then calls Torah a סם חיים: הקדוש ברוך הוא created the יצר הרע and created Torah as its remedy. Several teachings follow on how strong the יצר הרע is, and they end with the advice to drag it into the בית המדרש. The גמרא then returns to the ברייתא's list of a father's duties: marrying off his children, teaching his son a trade, and, according to some, teaching him to swim. Next it explains the משנה: both sons and daughters must honor and fear their parents, though a married woman is limited by her duties to her husband. A ברייתא compares honoring, fearing and cursing parents to the same acts toward הקדוש ברוך הוא, since all three are partners in a person. The עמוד ends with רבי beginning to explain why a son naturally honors his mother more, and the reason continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A chain of verses about sharp, ready Torah knowledge
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists several פסוקים showing that Torah should be as familiar and as sharp as arrows.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Say to wisdom: You are my sister.' And it says: 'Bind them on your fingers, write them on the tablet of your heart.' And it says: 'Like arrows in a warrior's hand, so are the children of youth.' And: 'Sharp arrows of the mighty.' And: 'Your arrows are sharp, peoples fall under you.' And: 'Happy is the man who filled his quiver with them; they will not be ashamed when they speak with enemies in the gate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps adding פסוקים to support one idea: Torah must be known clearly and be ready to use, like a sharp arrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling wisdom 'my sister' means knowing Torah as surely as you know who your sister is. The arrow verses compare Torah scholars to sharp arrows, always ready. The last verse, about 'enemies in the gate,' is the one the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says: introduces another supporting פסוק
Quiver, a case for holding arrows

phrases.english: "Say to wisdom: You are my sister, etc."
phrases.notes: משלי 7:4

phrases.english: And it says: "Bind them upon your fingers,
write them upon the tablet of your heart."
And it says: "Like arrows in the hand of a warrior,
so are the children of youth."
And it says: "Sharp arrows of the mighty."
And it says: "Your arrows are sharp,
peoples fall under you."
And it says: "Happy is the man
who has filled his quiver with them;
they shall not be ashamed when they speak
with enemies in the gate."
phrases.notes: תהלים 127:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of verses from the previous section of the דף.
steps.raayaObject: That Torah must be known clearly and be sharp and ready

steps.title: What are 'enemies in the gate'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'enemies in the gate' has to do with Torah study.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'enemies in the gate'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops at the last פסוק and asks what 'enemies' means here. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about Torah scholars, so speaking with 'enemies' sounds strange. The גמרא wants to know who these enemies are in a Torah setting.

keyTerms.meaning: Gate, the place where learning and judging happened

phrases.english: What is meant by "with enemies in the gate"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the last פסוק quoted in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'enemies in the gate' in a Torah context

steps.title: Study partners argue like enemies but end as friends
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא explains that even a father and son, or a רב and his תלמיד, become 'enemies' in learning but do not leave until they love each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: Even a father and his son, or a teacher and his student, who learn Torah together in one gate become enemies of each other. But they do not leave there until they become lovers of each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers the question: the 'enemies' are study partners who argue hard over the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real learning means pushing back, even against your own father or teacher. These are not real enemies; the argument is about truth. The answer adds that they stay until they come to love each other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
Even a father and his son, a teacher and his student,
who are learning Torah in one gate,
become enemies of each other.
But they do not leave there

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁנַּעֲשִׂים אוֹהֲבִים זֶה אֶת זֶה
phrases.english: until they become lovers of each other,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'enemies' are study partners who argue intensely but end up loving each other.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'enemies' are not real enemies. They are learning partners who argue about the Torah, and the argument ends in love.

steps.title: A verse hints that love comes at the end
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא brings a פסוק and reads בְּסוּפָה (a place name) as בְּסוֹפָהּ, 'at its end,' to show that love comes at the end of the argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Vahev in Sufah.' Do not read it as 'in Sufah' but as 'at its end.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא supports his claim that the partners end up loving each other by reading a פסוק in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word והב is read as connected to אהבה, love. Then בְּסוּפָה, a place name, is read as בְּסוֹפָהּ, 'at its end.' Together: love comes at the end of the battle of learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read: a way of reading a word with different vowels to draw a lesson
A word in the פסוק read here as 'love'

phrases.english: as it is said: "Vahev in Sufah."
phrases.notes: במדבר 21:14. Here והב is understood as 'love', like the word אהבה.

phrases.english: Do not read "in Sufah" but rather "at its end."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the claim in step 3 that the argument ends in love.
steps.raayaObject: That study partners end up loving each other
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר כא:יד, read with אל תקרי
steps.whatToRemember: Fierce argument in learning is a good thing. Partners who fight over the Torah end up loving each other.

steps.title: Torah is compared to a medicine of life
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads ושמתם as סם תם, 'a perfect medicine,' and says Torah is like a סם חיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And you shall place' can be read as סם תם, a perfect medicine. Torah is compared to a medicine of life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא that uses the sound of the word ושמתם to teach that Torah is like medicine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ושמתם sounds like סם תם, 'a perfect medicine.' From this wordplay the ברייתא teaches that Torah is a סם חיים, a medicine that gives life. The next step explains this with a parable.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught: introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "And you shall place" can be read as "a perfect medicine."
phrases.notes: דברים 11:18. The word ושמתם is split into two sounds: סם (medicine) and תם (perfect).

phrases.english: The Torah is compared to a medicine of life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on a new theme: Torah as a remedy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah is compared to a medicine of life, learned from reading ושמתם as סם תם.

steps.title: The parable of the father and the bandage
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a parable: a father hits his son, puts a bandage on the wound, and tells him he is safe as long as the bandage stays on.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a man who hit his son hard and put a bandage on his wound. He told him: My son, as long as this bandage is on your wound, eat whatever you like, drink whatever you like, and bathe in hot or cold water, and do not be afraid. But if you take it off, it will fester.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a parable to explain how Torah works like medicine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the bandage on, the son can live a normal life with no fear. Taking it off makes the wound go bad. This sets up the lesson in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable, a story used to explain an idea

phrases.aramaic: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁהִכָּה אֶת בְּנוֹ מַכָּה גְּדוֹלָה
phrases.english: A parable: a person hit his son with a strong blow
and placed a bandage on his wound,
and said to him: My son,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהָרְטִיָּה זוֹ עַל מַכָּתְךָ
phrases.english: as long as this bandage is on your wound,
eat whatever you enjoy,
and drink whatever you enjoy,
and bathe in either hot water or cold water,
and you need not be afraid.
But if you remove it,
it will become a festering sore.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the wound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the claim in step 5 that Torah is a medicine of life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As long as the bandage stays on, the son is safe; removing it makes the wound fester.

steps.title: Torah is the remedy for the יצר הרע
steps.stepSummary: The parable is applied: הקדוש ברוך הוא created the יצר הרע and created Torah as its remedy, so whoever learns Torah is not handed over to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, הקדוש ברוך הוא said to ישראל: My children, I created the יצר הרע, and I created Torah as its remedy. If you are busy with Torah, you will not be handed over into its hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what the parable means: the wound is the יצר הרע, and the bandage is Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the son is safe while the bandage is on, a Jew is safe from the יצר הרע while he learns Torah. Torah does not remove the יצר הרע; it protects the person from being controlled by it.

keyTerms.meaning: The evil inclination, the pull toward sin
Literally 'spice'; here, a remedy that balances it out
So too: begins applying the parable

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: So too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:
My children, I created the evil inclination,
and I created for it the Torah as its remedy.
And if you are busy with Torah,
you will not be handed over into its hand,
phrases.notes: 'Its hand' means the יצר הרע's power.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the parable of step 6 to Torah and the יצר הרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah is the remedy for the יצר הרע; one who learns Torah is not given over to it.
steps.whatToRemember: The wound is the יצר הרע and the bandage is Torah. Keep learning and you stay protected; stop and the wound festers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the idea that learning Torah is the main protection against sin.

steps.title: A verse from בראשית as proof
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins proving its point from the פסוק 'If you do well, shall it not be lifted up?'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'If you do well, shall it not be lifted up?'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to support the claim that one who learns Torah is not controlled by the יצר הרע. Steps 9 and 10 continue reading the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק was said to קין about the יצר הרע. 'Doing well' is understood as learning Torah, which lifts a person above the יצר הרע. Steps 9 and 10 read the rest of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: as it is said: "If you do well, shall it not be lifted up?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 4:7. Steps 9 and 10 read the rest of this פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוק behind the claim in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That one who learns Torah is not handed over to the יצר הרע

steps.title: Without Torah, you are handed over to the evil inclination
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues reading the פסוק: if you don't learn Torah, you are handed over to the יצר הרע, as it says 'sin crouches at the door.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you do not busy yourselves with Torah, you are handed over into its power, as it says: 'Sin crouches at the door.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the other side of the coin. Without Torah, a person falls into the hands of the יצר הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that learning Torah ('if you do well') lifts a person up. Now the next words of the same פסוק, 'sin crouches at the door,' show the danger of not learning: sin is waiting right there to take over. This fits the bandage parable, because taking off the bandage leaves the wound open.

phrases.english: And if you do not busy yourselves with Torah,
you are handed over into its hand,
phrases.notes: 'Its hand' means the יצר הרע's power, the same idea as the bandage parable in step 6.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Sin crouches at the door.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 4:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 8 by reading the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: Not learning Torah leaves a person handed over to the יצר הרע.

steps.title: The evil inclination focuses on you, but you can rule over it
steps.stepSummary: All of the יצר הרע's efforts are aimed at you ('to you is its desire'), yet if you want, you can rule over it ('and you shall rule over it').
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but all of its dealings are with you, as it says: 'And to you is its desire.' And if you want, you can rule over it, as it says: 'And you shall rule over it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads the rest of the same פסוק. The יצר הרע is fully focused on you, but you still have the power to control it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two new points are added from the end of the פסוק. First, the יצר הרע's whole 'business' is with the person. Second, the person is not helpless: if he chooses, he can master it. That ends the ברייתא's lesson on a hopeful note.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole פסוק of קין is read as a lesson about the יצר הרע: Torah lifts you up, without it sin waits at the door, and you can still choose to rule over it.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
all of its dealings are with you,
phrases.notes: Literally 'its carrying and giving,' which is a way of saying its business.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And to you is its desire.'
And if you want,
you rule over it,
as it says: 'And you shall rule over it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁכׇּל מַשָּׂאוֹ וּמַתָּנוֹ בְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק, adding two more points.
steps.raayaObject: The יצר הרע targets the person fully, but the person can master it.

steps.title: Even its Creator calls the evil inclination evil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the יצר הרע is so harsh that even הקדוש ברוך הוא, who created it, called it 'evil.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The evil inclination is so harsh that even its Creator called it evil, as it says: 'For the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about how strong and bad the יצר הרע is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that in the פסוק, הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself describes man's inclination as 'evil.' If even the One who made it calls it bad, it must be really bad. This opens a series of teachings about the יצר הרע's power.

keyTerms.meaning: its Creator, the One who formed it

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The evil inclination is harsh,
for even its Creator called it evil,
as it says: 'For the inclination of man's heart'
is evil from his youth.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:21. ה׳ is the one saying these words in the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of teachings about how strong the יצר הרע is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע is so bad that its Creator calls it evil.

steps.title: The evil inclination renews itself every day
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק teaches that a person's יצר הרע comes back fresh against him every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק said: A person's inclination renews itself against him every day, as it says: 'only evil all the day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק adds that the יצר הרע doesn't get tired. It starts over fresh each day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the words 'כל היום' (all the day) as 'every day.' So beating the יצר הרע yesterday does not finish the battle; it returns new today.

keyTerms.meaning: all the day, read here as 'every day'

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak said:
A person's inclination
renews itself against him every day,
as it says: 'only evil all the day.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:5

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק: יִצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְחַדֵּשׁ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another fact about the יצר הרע: it returns daily.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע renews itself against a person every day.

steps.title: The evil inclination tries to kill a person daily, and only ה׳'s help saves him
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לוי teaches that the יצר הרע overpowers a person every day and seeks to kill him, and without הקדוש ברוך הוא's help he could not beat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן לוי said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says: 'The wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to kill him.' And if הקדוש ברוך הוא did not help him, he could not overcome it, as it says: 'God will not leave him in its hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן לוי makes the danger even stronger: the יצר הרע doesn't just return, it attacks and wants to kill. Then he adds the comfort that ה׳ helps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the 'wicked one' in תהלים as the יצר הרע, and the 'righteous' as the person. The very next פסוק says God won't leave him in its hand. That teaches that a person cannot win alone, but with הקדוש ברוך הוא's help he can.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: יִצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו בְּכׇל יוֹם
phrases.english: A person's inclination overpowers him every day
and seeks to kill him,
as it says: 'The wicked one watches the righteous'
and seeks to kill him,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 37:32. Here 'the wicked one' is read as the יצר הרע.

phrases.english: And if the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not help him,
he could not overcome it,
as it says: 'God will not leave him in its hand.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 37:33, the very next פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לֵוִי: יִצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב יצחק: the יצר הרע not only renews daily but attacks to kill, and ה׳'s help is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע tries to destroy a person daily, and he can beat it only with הקדוש ברוך הוא's help.

steps.title: Drag the evil inclination into the study hall, where Torah breaks it
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches: if the יצר הרע meets you, pull it into the בית המדרש. If it's stone it melts, if it's iron it shatters, as Torah is like fire and a hammer that smashes rock.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל: My son, if this disgusting one meets you, drag it to the study hall. If it is stone, it melts; if it is iron, it shatters, as it says: 'Is not My word like fire, says ה׳, and like a hammer that shatters rock?'
steps.whatsHappening: After describing how dangerous the יצר הרע is, the גמרא gives the practical solution: go learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: However hard the יצר הרע is, like stone or even iron, Torah is stronger. The פסוק from ירמיהו compares ה׳'s word to fire and a hammer, which can break the hardest things. This ties back to step 7: Torah is the remedy for the יצר הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line of the whole discussion: the way to fight the יצר הרע is to go learn Torah.

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנִי אִם פָּגַע בְּךָ מְנֻוּוֹל זֶה –
phrases.english: My son, if this disgusting one meets you,
phrases.notes: 'This disgusting one' is the יצר הרע.

phrases.english: drag it to the study hall.
If it is stone, it melts,
and if it is iron, it shatters,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ נְאֻם ה׳
phrases.english: as it says: 'Is not My word like fire, says ה׳,
and like a hammer that shatters rock?'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 23:29. This פסוק backs up the iron half: Torah smashes even the hardest thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: בְּנִי אִם פָּגַע בְּךָ מְנֻוּוֹל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the warnings about the יצר הרע's strength, gives the practical cure: Torah study.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bring the יצר הרע into the בית המדרש; Torah melts it or shatters it.

steps.title: Proof that Torah melts the stone: water wears away stones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the 'stone melts' half: Torah is called water, and water wears away stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is stone, it melts, as it says: 'Ho, all who thirst, come to the water,' and it says: 'Water wears away stones.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first half of the teaching, the stone that melts, and gives it its own proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים are joined. ישעיהו calls Torah 'water,' and איוב says water wears down stones. So Torah, like water, slowly wears down even a stone-hard יצר הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: and it also says (brings a second פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The יצר הרע is strong and returns every day, but Torah is its remedy: like a hammer it shatters iron, and like water it wears down stone.

phrases.english: If it is stone, it melts,
as it says: 'Ho, all who thirst, come to the water,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 55:1. Here 'water' means Torah.

phrases.english: and it says: 'Water wears away stones.'
phrases.notes: איוב 14:19

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֶבֶן הוּא – נִימּוֹחַ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הוֹי כׇּל צָמֵא לְכוּ לַמַּיִם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for the 'stone melts' half of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: Torah melts a stone-like יצר הרע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 55:1 (Torah is water) combined with איוב 14:19 (water wears away stones)

steps.title: Where do we learn that a father must marry off his son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the ברייתא, a father's duty to marry off his son, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said a father must find his son a wife. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of a father's duties in the ברייתא and asks where this one comes from. This is a setup line; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this were a side-discussion about Torah study and the יצר הרע. Now the גמרא picks up the ברייתא's list again and asks for a source for the item 'to marry him off to a woman.'

keyTerms.meaning: To marry him off to a woman, to help his son get married
From where do we know this? (asking for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't connect this to the יצר הרע discussion just before it. The גמרא has gone back to the ברייתא's list of what a father owes his son.

phrases.english: To marry him off to a woman.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the ברייתא on 29a that lists what a father must do for his son.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יצר הרע discussion and returns to the ברייתא's list of a father's duties.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for a father's duty to marry off his son.

steps.title: The source: ירמיהו tells parents to marry off their children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites ירמיהו 29:6, which tells parents to take wives for their sons and give their daughters to husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The source is the פסוק: 'Take wives and have sons and daughters; take wives for your sons and give your daughters to men.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a פסוק in ירמיהו that tells parents to arrange marriages for their children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'take wives for your sons' directly command parents to see that their sons get married. The same פסוק also mentions daughters, and the next step asks about that part.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introducing a פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Take wives and bear sons and daughters,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 29:6

phrases.english: and take wives for your sons,
and give your daughters to men."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ירמיהו 29:6 commands parents to take wives for their sons.

steps.title: How can a father make his daughter get married?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a father can tell his son to go marry, but how can he control whether a man comes to marry his daughter?
steps.simpleTranslation: A son makes sense, because his father can tell him to go find a wife. But a daughter? That isn't in the father's hands, since she has to wait for a man to choose her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second half of the פסוק, which tells parents to 'give' their daughters to men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those days the man was the one who acted to get married, so a father could push his son to do it. A daughter depended on someone else choosing her, so how could the נביא command something the father cannot control?

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense (setting up a contrast)
In his hands, within his control

phrases.english: Granted, his son – that is in his hands,
but his daughter – is that in his hands?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּנוֹ – בְּיָדוֹ, אֶלָּא בִּתּוֹ – בְּיָדוֹ הִיא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how to read the daughters half of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'give your daughters to men' in ירמיהו 29:6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A command must be something a person can do, but a daughter's marriage is not in the father's control.

steps.title: Give her a dowry and dress her well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the father should give his daughter a dowry and good clothing so that men will be eager to marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the נביא meant: the father should give her something, dress her and cover her nicely, so that men will jump at the chance to marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what 'give your daughters' really asks of the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father cannot force a match, but he can make one likely. Giving her money or goods and dressing her well is the part that is in his hands, and that is what the פסוק commands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant (reinterpreting the words)
Something, here a gift or dowry
They will jump at her, eagerly seek to marry her

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of the ירמיהו פסוק are real duties: a father pushes his son to marry, and makes his daughter attractive to marry by giving her a dowry and good clothing.

phrases.english: This is what he was saying to them:
he should give her something
and dress her and cover her
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

phrases.english: so that men will jump at her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about daughters.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the command so that it covers what is in the father's control
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Give your daughters' means the father must actually make the marriage happen, which he cannot do.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means he must give her a dowry and clothing so that men will want to marry her.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a father must teach his son a trade?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the ברייתא, teaching one's son a trade, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said a father must teach his son a trade. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the ברייתא's list and asks for its source. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as step 16: quote an item from the ברייתא, then ask 'מנלן'.

keyTerms.meaning: A trade or craft, a way to make a living

phrases.english: To teach him a trade.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next duty listed in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for a father's duty to teach his son a trade.

steps.title: חזקיה: 'See life with the woman you love'
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה derives the duty from קהלת 9:9 and shows it works whether 'woman' means a real wife or the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said the source is 'See life with the woman you love.' If 'woman' means a real wife, then just as a father must find his son a wife, he must also teach him a trade so he can have a living. If 'woman' means the תורה, then just as a father must teach his son תורה, he must also teach him a trade.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives a פסוק as the source and explains that it teaches the duty under either reading of the word 'woman'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'life', meaning a livelihood, next to 'woman'. Whatever the 'woman' stands for, wife or תורה, is something a father must give his son, and the 'life' attached to it, a trade, is put on the same level.

keyTerms.meaning: See life, enjoy life; read here as making a living

steps.whatToRemember: Teaching a trade is a real duty of a father, placed alongside finding his son a wife and teaching him תורה.

phrases.english: Chizkiyah said:
As the verse says:
"See life with the woman whom you love."
phrases.notes: קהלת 9:9

phrases.english: If it means an actual woman:
just as he must marry him off to a woman,
so too he must teach him a trade.
If it means the Torah:
just as he must teach him Torah,
so too he must teach him a trade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source for teaching a trade.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קהלת 9:9 links 'life' (a livelihood) to the 'woman', so under either reading a trade is a father's duty.

steps.title: Some say: teach him to swim, but why?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's last opinion, that a father must also teach his son to swim, and asks the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the father must also teach his son to swim in a river. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last opinion in the ברייתא and asks why swimming belongs on the list. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier items, here the גמרא does not ask for a פסוק ('מנלן'). It asks for a reason ('מאי טעמא'), because this duty is based on logic.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach him to swim in a river

phrases.english: And some say: also to teach him to swim in a river.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים אַף לַהֲשִׁיטוֹ בַּנָּהָר. מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the final opinion in the ברייתא's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a father must teach his son to swim.

steps.title: Swimming can save his life
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that swimming is needed for the son's life, since it could save him from drowning.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is his life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that knowing how to swim can save the son's life, so a father must teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No פסוק is needed. Protecting the son's life is reason enough, so swimming is on the list next to marriage, a trade and תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: His life, what keeps him alive

steps.whatToRemember: A father's duties cover his son's whole life: a wife, a livelihood, תורה, and, according to some, even the skill to save himself from drowning.

phrases.english: It is his life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why swimming is a father's duty.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Swimming can save the son's life.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: no trade means teaching banditry
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that a father who does not teach his son a trade teaches him banditry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Any father who does not teach his son a trade teaches him banditry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another opinion from the same ברייתא about a father's duties. רבי יהודה gives a sharp warning about not teaching a son a trade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion already said a father must teach his son a trade. רבי יהודה adds strong language: a son with no way to earn a living may end up stealing. This sets up the next two questions: does he really mean banditry, and how is he different from the first opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: A trade or craft, a skill used to earn a living

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Any father who does not teach him a trade
teaches him banditry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא about a father's duties, now giving רבי יהודה's opinion on teaching a trade.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father who does not teach his son a trade is held responsible as if he taught him banditry.

steps.title: Can he really be teaching banditry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: surely the father is not literally teaching his son to rob.
steps.simpleTranslation: Banditry? Could that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יהודה's words. A father who simply fails to teach a trade is not actually giving lessons in robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, רבי יהודה's words make no sense, because doing nothing is not the same as teaching crime. The גמרא points out this problem so it can explain what he really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? A way of saying 'that can't be right'

phrases.english: Banditry? Could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal wording of רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word מְלַמְּדוֹ לִיסְטוּת in רבי יהודה's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A father who doesn't teach a trade is not actively teaching robbery, so the literal wording can't be right.

steps.title: It is as if he taught him banditry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה means it is as though the father taught him banditry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is as if he teaches him banditry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה was speaking in a 'like' sense, not a literal one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding one word, כאילו ('as if'), fixes the problem. The father doesn't teach crime, but by leaving his son without a living he sets him up to steal, so he is blamed as though he had taught it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is as if he teaches him banditry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection by reading רבי יהודה's statement as a comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to say the father literally teaches robbery.
steps.terutzMaskana: He means the father is considered as if he taught robbery, since his son will likely turn to it.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה differs from the first opinion, since both require teaching a trade.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking what practical difference there is between the first opinion and רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions say a father must teach his son a trade. If they agree, why does the ברייתא record two opinions? The גמרא wants a case where they would rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the first opinion in the ברייתא, that a father must teach his son a trade, and רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After clarifying רבי יהודה's wording, the גמרא asks how his view differs from the first opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the first opinion and רבי יהודה would disagree.

steps.title: The difference: teaching him business
steps.stepSummary: They differ when the father teaches his son business instead of a craft.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them where he taught him business.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions disagree when the father teaches his son to do business rather than a hands-on trade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first opinion, business counts as a way to earn a living, so it is enough. רבי יהודה holds that business is not enough; the son needs a real craft, or else it is as if he was taught banditry.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he taught him business.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by naming the case where the opinions differ.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the father teaches his son business: the first opinion says that is enough, and רבי יהודה requires an actual trade.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees a father must make sure his son can earn a living. The argument is only whether business is enough (first opinion) or a real craft is needed (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: What does 'all מצוות of the father on the son' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks what the phrase 'all מצוות of the father on the son' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'All מצוות of the father on the son,' and so on. What does 'all מצוות of the father on the son' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of our משנה and asks what this unclear phrase means. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says men and women are both obligated in 'all מצוות of the father on the son.' The wording can be read two ways: duties a father owes his son, or duties a son owes his father. The גמרא needs to decide which one.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the מצוות of the father on the son'; the meaning is unclear
Et cetera; the quote continues as in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִצְוֹת הָאָב עַל הַבֵּן וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'All מצוות of the father on the son,' and so on.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי כׇּל מִצְוֹת הָאָב עַל הַבֵּן?
phrases.english: What is meant by 'all מצוות of the father on the son'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כׇּל מִצְוֹת הָאָב עַל הַבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא about a father's duties and returns to explain the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the phrase means duties a father owes his son or duties a son owes his father.

steps.title: Women aren't obligated in מילה and פדיון
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה means duties a father owes his son, that clashes with a ברייתא saying only the father must do מילה and פדיון הבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means every מצוה a father must do for his son, and women are obligated in them, isn't it taught: 'The father is obligated to circumcise his son and to redeem him'? That means his father, yes; his mother, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first reading, duties a father owes his son, and shows it can't be right because a ברייתא says the mother is not obligated in them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'the father' must do מילה and פדיון הבן for his son, which implies the mother does not have to. But under this reading, the משנה says women are obligated too. The two sources contradict, so this reading fails.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a possible reading that will be rejected
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: If you say that it means every מצוה
that a father is obligated to do for his son
women are obligated?
phrases.notes: Read this as a surprised question: would women really be obligated in those?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
The father is obligated regarding his son
to circumcise him and to redeem him.
His father, yes; his mother, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא כֹּל מִצְוָתָא דְּמִיחַיַּיב אַבָּא לְמִיעְבַּד לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible reading of the משנה and rejects it with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as duties a father owes his son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא puts מילה and פדיון only on the father, so women can't be obligated in duties toward a son as the משנה would then say.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'מצוות of the father' looks like it means what the father must do. The גמרא is about to show it actually means what is done for the father.

steps.title: רב יהודה: מצוות a child owes to his father
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the משנה means the מצוות a child must do for his father, and in these both sons and daughters are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what the משנה means: all מצוות for the father that are placed on the son to do for his father, both men and women are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the correct reading of the משנה: it is talking about the child's duties toward the parent, not the parent's duties toward the child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By reading 'מצוות of the father' as 'מצוות done for the father,' the contradiction disappears. Honoring and fearing a parent apply to sons and daughters alike, while מילה and פדיון (duties toward a son) remain on the father alone.

keyTerms.meaning: That are placed on the son

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it means:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִצְוֹת הָאָב הַמּוּטָּלֹת עַל הַבֵּן
phrases.english: All מצוות for the father that are placed on the son
to do for his father,
both men and women are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction by giving a new reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to obligate women in duties a parent owes a child, like מילה and פדיון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means duties a child owes a parent, like honor and fear, which apply to sons and daughters equally.
steps.whatToRemember: 'מצוות of the father on the son' means the child's duties toward the parent. Both sons and daughters must honor and fear their parents.

steps.title: Already taught: 'You shall fear' includes women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב יהודה's point was already taught in a ברייתא learning from the plural word תיראו that women must fear parents too.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this, as the רבנן taught: 'A man' — I only know a man; from where do I know a woman? When it says 'you shall fear' in the plural, there are two here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא already said what רב יהודה said: daughters, not just sons, must fear their parents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק begins with the singular word 'man,' which seems to leave out women. But the verb תיראו is plural, so the ברייתא learns that two kinds of people are meant: men and women. This supports רב יהודה's reading that women share in the child's duties toward parents.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know; the text by itself teaches only this

phrases.english: We already learned this
as the Rabbis taught in a ברייתא:
'A man' — I only know a man;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:3: 'A man shall fear his mother and his father.'

phrases.english: from where do I know a woman?
When it says 'you shall fear',
phrases.notes: The verb is plural, even though 'a man' is singular. That plural word is the hint.

phrases.english: there are two here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's reading by showing a ברייתא already taught it.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's statement that women share in the child's duties toward parents
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 19:3, where the plural תיראו includes women alongside 'a man'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that daughters, not only sons, must fear their parents, a basic rule in the laws of honoring parents.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'man'?
steps.stepSummary: If women must also fear their parents, why does the פסוק use the word איש?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the verse teach by saying 'man'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own conclusion. If women are obligated too, the word 'man' seems out of place. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 32 the plural word תיראו showed that women are included. But the same פסוק opens with איש, which sounds like only men are meant. The ברייתא must explain why that word is there.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
What does the verse come to teach?

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying 'man'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word איש in the very פסוק that step 32 used to include women.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that women must fear parents just as men do
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says איש, which suggests only men are obligated.

steps.title: A man is always free to act; a married woman is not
steps.stepSummary: The word איש teaches that a man can always do this מצוה, while a married woman cannot always do it because she answers to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man has the ability to do it. A woman does not always have the ability to do it, because she is under the authority of others.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. The word 'man' does not leave women out. It teaches who is always able to carry out the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman's obligation stays the same. But in practice a married woman has duties to her husband's household and is not always free to serve her parents. The word איש points to the person who is always free to act.

keyTerms.meaning: It is in his power; he is able

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean women are exempt. They are fully obligated. The point is only that a married woman is not always able to carry it out.

phrases.english: A man has it in his power to do it,
a woman does not have it in her power to do it,
because the authority of others is upon her.
phrases.notes: 'Others' here means her husband, whose household she has to look after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word איש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the word: it describes who is able to act, not who is obligated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word איש would mean only men are obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are obligated. איש points to the man because he is always free to do it.

steps.title: A divorced woman is equal to a son
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that once a woman is divorced, she and a son are equally bound to honor and fear their parents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב: If she was divorced, both of them are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב draws a practical result from the previous answer. Once the husband's claim on her time is gone, the daughter is just like the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only thing holding the married woman back was her husband's authority. A divorce removes that, so nothing is left to separate her from a son in this מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The two of them are equal

steps.whatToRemember: Sons and daughters are both obligated to honor and fear parents. A married daughter is limited only by her duties to her husband. Once she is divorced, she and a son are equal.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said that Rav said:
If she was divorced, both of them are equal.
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means the daughter and the son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a practical ruling on the reason given in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A divorced daughter is obligated in honoring and fearing parents exactly like a son.

steps.title: Honoring parents is compared to honoring the הקב"ה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the same word כבד is used for parents and for the הקב"ה, so the תורה puts honoring parents on the same level.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: It says 'Honor your father and your mother,' and it says 'Honor the Lord with your wealth.' The verse compares honoring father and mother to honoring the Omnipresent.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא begins. It points to the shared word 'honor' in two פסוקים to show how great כיבוד אב ואם is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the same command, כבד. The תורה uses one word for both, and this shows that honoring parents is placed alongside honoring the הקב"ה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Omnipresent; a name for the הקב"ה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
It is said: 'Honor your father and your mother,'
phrases.notes: שמות 20:11

phrases.english: and it is said: 'Honor the Lord with your wealth.'
phrases.notes: משלי 3:9

phrases.english: The verse equated honoring father and mother
to honoring the Omnipresent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about how great the מצוה of honoring parents is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honoring parents is placed on the same level as honoring the הקב"ה.

steps.title: Fearing parents is compared to fearing the הקב"ה
steps.stepSummary: The same pattern applies to fear: the word תירא is used both for parents and for the הקב"ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says 'A man shall fear his mother and his father,' and it says 'You shall fear the Lord your God and serve Him.' The verse compares fearing father and mother to fearing the Omnipresent.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats its pattern, this time with fear instead of honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the shared word is the root of fear (ירא). Just as with honor, the parallel wording places fearing parents alongside fearing the הקב"ה.

phrases.english: It is said: 'A man shall fear his mother and his father,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:3

phrases.aramaic: וְנֶאֱמַר: ״אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּירָא וְאֹתוֹ תַעֲבֹד״,
phrases.english: and it is said: 'You shall fear the Lord your God and Him you shall serve.'
phrases.notes: דברים 6:13

phrases.english: The verse equated fearing father and mother
to fearing the Omnipresent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second comparison in the same ברייתא, now about fear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fearing parents is placed on the same level as fearing the הקב"ה.

steps.title: Cursing parents is compared to cursing the הקב"ה
steps.stepSummary: The verb קלל is used both for cursing parents and for cursing the הקב"ה, so the תורה compares the two.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says 'One who curses his father or his mother shall be put to death,' and it says 'Any man who curses his God shall bear his sin.' The verse compares 'blessing' father and mother to 'blessing' the Omnipresent.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא makes its third comparison, this time with cursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same verb, קלל, appears in both פסוקים, so the sin of cursing parents is compared to cursing the הקב"ה. The ברייתא says 'blessing' instead of 'cursing' so as not to speak of cursing the הקב"ה directly.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall surely be put to death
'Blessing of', a polite way of saying cursing

steps.confusionAlert: The word ברכה here does not mean a real blessing. It is a polite way of saying 'cursing.'

phrases.english: It is said: 'One who curses his father or his mother shall be put to death,'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:17

phrases.aramaic: וְנֶאֱמַר: ״אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי יְקַלֵּל אֱלֹהָיו וְנָשָׂא חֶטְאוֹ״,
phrases.english: and it is said: 'Any man who curses his God shall bear his sin.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:15

phrases.english: The verse equated 'blessing' father and mother
to 'blessing' the Omnipresent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third comparison in the same ברייתא, now about cursing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cursing parents is compared to cursing the הקב"ה.

steps.title: Striking cannot be compared
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by noting that hitting a parent has no parallel with the הקב"ה, because striking Him is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with striking, it is certainly impossible.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by pointing out where the comparison stops. A person can strike a parent, but there is no way to strike the הקב"ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה also has a death penalty for striking a parent, so one might expect a fourth comparison. The ברייתא explains that none can exist, since hitting the הקב"ה is not possible at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The תורה compares honor, fear and cursing of parents to honor, fear and cursing of the הקב"ה. Only striking has no parallel, because striking Him is impossible.

phrases.english: But with striking, it is certainly impossible.
phrases.notes: He means you can't compare striking a parent to striking the הקב"ה, since no one can hit Him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Marks the limit of the three comparisons just made.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Honor, fear and cursing are compared between parents and the הקב"ה, but striking cannot be compared.

steps.title: The reason for the comparison: three partners
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that it is logical to compare parents to the הקב"ה, because all three are partners in a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is logical, because the three of them are partners in him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous steps finishes by giving a reason for its comparisons. Parents and the הקב"ה are treated alike because all three take part in making a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 36-38 showed from the wording of the פסוקים that כיבוד, מורא, and קללה of parents are compared to the הקב"ה. Now the ברייתא adds that this also makes sense on its own logic. Since all three are partners in a person, honoring one partner is like honoring the others.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it is logical; this also makes sense on its own

phrases.english: And so too it is logical,
since the three of them are partners in him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a logical reason for the comparisons the ברייתא drew from the wording of the פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comparing parents to the הקב"ה is logical, because all three are partners in creating a person.

steps.title: The three partners in a person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the הקב"ה, the father, and the mother are partners in a person. When someone honors his parents, the הקב"ה counts it as if they honored Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There are three partners in a person: the הקב"ה, his father, and his mother. When a person honors his father and mother, the הקב"ה says: I consider it as if I lived among them and they honored Me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out the idea of the 'three partners.' It shows what that partnership means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 40 only mentioned that the three are partners. This ברייתא names them and adds something new: honoring parents is credited as honoring the הקב"ה Himself. This is why כיבוד אב ואם is put on the same level as honoring the הקב"ה.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught; this introduces a ברייתא
I consider it for them; I count it to their credit

steps.whatToRemember: Honoring your parents counts as honoring the הקב"ה, because He is their partner in creating you.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the basic reason why כיבוד אב ואם is so serious: it is tied directly to honoring the הקב"ה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There are three partners in a person:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, his father, and his mother.
When a person honors
his father and his mother,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, says:
I credit them
as if I lived among them and they honored Me.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה שׁוּתָּפִין הֵן בָּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that spells out and supports the 'three partners' reasoning of step 40.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that parents and the הקב"ה are partners, so honoring parents is like honoring the הקב"ה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תנו רבנן) listing the three partners and the הקב"ה's statement that He counts honoring parents as honoring Him.

steps.title: רבי: a son naturally honors his mother more
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that the הקב"ה knows a son honors his mother more than his father. The reason begins here and continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי says: It is revealed and known before the One Who spoke and the world came into being that a son honors his mother more than his father, because...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא from רבי about how a child naturally treats each parent. This line sets up the next move, because the reason ("because...") continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא compared parents to the הקב"ה. Now רבי adds a new point about the two parents themselves: by nature, a son leans toward honoring his mother more. This sets up an explanation of how the תורה deals with that natural tendency.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The One Who spoke and the world came into being; a name for the הקב"ה

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: It is revealed and known before
the One Who spoke and the world came into being
that a son honors his mother
more than his father, because
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next עמוד, where the reason is given.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: By nature, a son honors his mother more than his father. The reason continues on the next עמוד.
